text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — elevated 5xx for /v1/embeddings in eu-west-1 (rate ~18% over baseline). Alert window: 2026-03-15T10:12Z. PagerDuty: PD-1248. Link: https://alerts.internal/redwood/PD-1248

oncall_sre: Acked. I'm on it. Any obvious customer-reported impacts?

maria_g: seeing customer error spikes in prod. Examples: several SaaS customers hitting embedding endpoints get 500s + `incompatible_response_type`. Started ~10:11Z. Logs show responses coming from runtime `redwood-instruct` for embed requests.

samir_k: that smells like an alias/routing mismatch — maybe a release anchored an alias to the wrong model family. Can someone check current alias mappings and fallback rules for the `embeddings` interface?

kevin_p: running the quick inspect:
```
# internal tool
$ infractl routing get --alias stable-embeds --region eu-west-1
alias: stable-embeds
bound_model: redwood-instruct-v2
interface: gen/instruct
pinned_at: 2026-03-15T10:09Z
fallback_policy: allow_compatible_variants
```
Output shows alias is bound to an instruct model — that's our issue. The alias was updated as part of 10:08Z release (deploy 2026-03-15T10:05Z) and got mis-anchored.

oncall_sre: confirmed. Embedding requests are being routed to an instruct variant, runtime rejects request (type mismatch) and some code paths return 500. This explains errors.

maria_g: customer-facing impact — at least 3 paying customers reported failures; estimate ~2.4k requests/min failing during the peak. SLO: embedding success 99.9% — looks like a short SLO miss window.

samir_k: suggested mitigations: 1) temporarily block instruct-family fallback for `embeddings` interface, 2) rebind alias to correct embed model `redwood-embed-v2`, 3) monitor 5xx and latencies, 4) notify customers. Which one to do first?

oncall_sre: I'll do (1) and (2) in that order to avoid further cross-interface hits. Executing now.

eng-runtime-bot: Applying policy change: `modify fallback_policy stable-embeds -> disallow_cross_interface`
eng-runtime-bot: Policy change applied (txn id tx-9882).

kevin_p: Rebinding alias now:
```
$ infractl routing bind --alias stable-embeds --model redwood-embed-v2 --region eu-west-1
2026-03-15T10:16:38Z binding updated: stable-embeds -> redwood-embed-v2
```

oncall_sre: Rollback/bind done. Watching metrics...

pagerduty-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation step recorded. Escalation: mitigated -> investigating.

maria_g: 5xx rate dropping fast, now down to ~1.5% and falling. Latency stable. Customer errors resolved in reported accounts — support ticket updates queued.

samir_k: Good. Short-term mitigation complete. Need root cause: why did deploy bind alias to wrong model? Was it a bad deploy artifact or automation bug?

oncall_sre: early hypothesis: release pipeline's alias mapping step used a template param that defaulted to a `model_family` value (gen/instruct) for that deploy. File: infra/releases/2026-03-15/release.yaml shows `alias_bindings: stable-embeds: $MODEL_FAMILY-latest` and an env var was set incorrectly.

kevin_p: grabbing the release job logs. Found: `RELEASE_MODEL_FAMILY=redwood-instruct` exported in CI job by mistake at 10:05Z. The job applied alias bindings as part of the release.

samir_k: action items: (A) CI fix to enforce interface sanity check (disallow binding gen/instruct to embedding alias), (B) add integration test in release pipeline to validate alias -> interface compatibility, (C) run a sweep to find any other aliases mis-bound in last 24h, (D) customer comms + PMR.

oncall_sre: created incident ticket INC-2026-1248 and assigned samir_k as postmortem owner. I've also opened a support notice draft to be sent to affected customers; will coordinate with maria for wording.

maria_g: customer impact summary for comms: 3 customers impacted, ~12 minutes of elevated errors (10:11Z-10:23Z), estimated 28k requests affected total. No data exposure. Apologies emphasized.

samir_k: I'm putting a short-term safety guard: publishing a cluster-side policy to reject cross-interface bindings from CI unless flagged. Will PR in 5 mins.

eng-runtime-bot: Cluster policy applied: `prevent_cross_interface_binding=true` (scope: release CI).

oncall_sre: closing pager duty incident as mitigated but leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. We should schedule a 1-hour blameless postmortem tomorrow and RCA doc.

maria_g: will send customer notices from support channel once postmortem plan approved.

samir_k: thanks team. Follow-ups: PR for CI check (owner: samir_k), integration test (owner: kevin_p), sweeping audit (owner: oncall_sre). ETA: 48 hours.

oncall_sre: Noted. Posting retrospective invite. :calendar: 

pagerduty-bot: PD incident transitioned to "resolved (mitigated)" at 2026-03-15T10:25Z.

kevin_p: Quick note — there are no further 5xx clusters in other regions. Will run the sweep across all aliases to ensure no duplicate mis-anchors.

maria_g: thanks all. closing channel for now, will reopen if we see regression. :thumbsup:
